title: Extension of scalars at a ringed topos point
statement: Let C be a small site, A and R sheaves of commutative rings on C, c:A→R a ring-sheaf morphism [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus], p:Set→Sh(C) a point [def-trf-geometric-morphism], and a and s normalized ring/module stalk presentations [def-sfb-ringed-site-point] for A and R at p. There is a ring homomorphism b:a.ring→s.ring whose underlying function is the stalk of c under the specified ring identifications. For every A-module sheaf N [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] there is a natural additive equivalence s.modules(R⊗_A N) ≃ a.modules(N)⊗_{a.ring}s.ring [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. It is s.ring-linear for the action on the last factor transported by tensor symmetry. For every generalized pair of sections r of R and m of N and their sheafified pure tensor z, its value on the germ of z is m_p⊗r_p. The ring map is normalized on every element of p⁻¹A, and the equivalences commute with every A-module morphism. All objects and values use the common universe [def-weil-size-convention].

source.place: Tag 05V5, lemma-pullback-stalk, proof; Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, proof.

proof.text: Apply the point inverse image to c. The ring graph equations for the two point presentations show that its underlying function preserves zero, one, addition and multiplication, including when a stalk ring is zero. Bundle this as b; its definition gives the normalization on every underlying stalk element.

source.place: Tag 05V5, lemma-pullback-stalk, proof; Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, proof.

proof.text: Present Set as sheaves on the one-object site with trivial topology, and identify module sheaves on it with ordinary modules. Transport the point presentation to an algebraic inverse image on this site. Apply the normalized inverse-image tensor comparison to R restricted along c and to N. The stalk of the restricted R-module is the target stalk ring restricted along b, by its scalar-operation graph. The sheaf tensor becomes the ordinary tensor under the one-object equivalence. Transport the point adjunction and finite-limit preservation through the sheaf equivalence. Forgetting extension of scalars to A-modules gives the sheaf tensor of restricted R with N, because both are sectionwise tensor followed by sheafification and represent the same sheaf bilinear maps. Its A-stalk is the restriction along b of the s-stalk, by the operation graphs and their underlying-set identifications.

source.place: Tag 05V5, lemma-pullback-stalk, proof; Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, proof.

proof.text: The generalized-section formula for the comparison identifies its value on the pure pairing with the tensor of the germs. Tensor symmetry puts the target stalk ring last. The action of R on the first factor transports to multiplication on its stalk; tensor universality therefore proves linearity for the action defined by symmetry. Naturality of the tensor comparison and symmetry gives the equation on every module map. The normalized generalized-section equation follows by the same symmetry.

lean.statement:
theorem RingedSitePoint.scalarExtension
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    (A R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (c : A ⟶ R)
    (p : GeometricMorphism (Type u) (Sheaf J (Type u)))
    (a : RingedSitePoint A p) (s : RingedSitePoint R p) :
    ∃ b : a.ring →+* s.ring,
      (∀ x : p.inverse.obj ((sheafCompose J (forget CommRingCat.{u})).obj A),
        b (a.ringUnderlying.hom x) = s.ringUnderlying.hom
          (p.inverse.map ((sheafCompose J (forget CommRingCat.{u})).map c) x)) ∧
      letI : Algebra a.ring s.ring := b.toAlgebra
      ∃ e : ∀ N : ringedSiteModules.{u} (ringSheaf A),
        s.modules.obj (changeOfRings.{u, u, u} c N) ≃+
          TensorProduct a.ring (a.modules.obj N) s.ring,
        (∀ (N : ringedSiteModules.{u} (ringSheaf A)) (r : s.ring)
          (x : s.modules.obj (changeOfRings.{u, u, u} c N)),
          e N (r • x) = TensorProduct.comm a.ring s.ring (a.modules.obj N)
            (r • TensorProduct.comm a.ring (a.modules.obj N) s.ring (e N x))) ∧
        (∀ (N N' : ringedSiteModules.{u} (ringSheaf A)) (h : N ⟶ N')
          (x : s.modules.obj (changeOfRings.{u, u, u} c N)),
          e N' (s.modules.map (changeOfRingsHom.{u, u, u} c N h) x) =
            TensorProduct.map (a.modules.map h).hom (LinearMap.id : s.ring →ₗ[a.ring] s.ring)
              (e N x)) ∧
        ∀ (N : ringedSiteModules.{u} (ringSheaf A)) (T : Sheaf J (Type u))
          (r : T ⟶ (sheafCompose J (forget CommRingCat.{u})).obj R)
          (m : T ⟶ (SheafOfModules.RingedTensor.underlying A).obj N)
          (z : T ⟶ (SheafOfModules.RingedTensor.underlying R).obj
            (changeOfRings.{u, u, u} c N)),
          (∀ (W : Cᵒᵖ) (x : T.obj.obj W),
            z.hom.app W x = ((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction.{u, u, u, u}
              (𝟙 (ringSheaf R).obj)).unit.app
                (changeOfRingsPresheaf.{u, u, u} c N)).app W
                  ((@id (R.obj.obj W) (r.hom.app W x))
                    ⊗ₜ[A.obj.obj W, (c.hom.app W).hom]
                      (@id (N.val.obj W) (m.hom.app W x)))) →
          ∀ x : p.inverse.obj T,
            e N ((s.moduleUnderlying.inv.app (changeOfRings.{u, u, u} c N))
              (p.inverse.map z x)) =
              ((a.moduleUnderlying.inv.app N) (p.inverse.map m x)) ⊗ₜ[a.ring]
                (s.ringUnderlying.hom (p.inverse.map r x))
